meta.source: Spider (Yu et al., 2018) dev+train-set questions + official gold SQL, xlangai/spider HuggingFace mirror -- verbatim, third-party authored, not hand-written for this project.
meta.purpose: Third evaluation domain (bike-sharing), selected via scripts/rank_all_spider_databases.py for join-free-friendliness against planner/'s 4-operator vocabulary. All 104 real questions come from Spider's TRAIN split (bike_1 has zero dev/validation coverage -- see scripts/combine_spider_train_dev.py); combined_data.parquet was needed to unblock this domain, dev_data.parquet alone has 0 bike_1 rows.
meta.register_table_note: The real bike_1 database has 4 tables (station, status, trip, weather). weather scored highest by raw column-richness (22 numeric columns) AND has slightly more real single-table questions (14 vs trip's 10) -- but weather is a temperature/humidity/wind/pressure log, not bike-sharing data; a domain literally named 'bike_1' whose answerable content was mostly about weather would be a confusing choice. 'trip' was chosen instead: genuinely about bike rides (duration, stations, subscriptions), a robust row count (9,959), and real categorical variety (subscription_type: Subscriber/Customer) -- at the cost of only 10 real single-table answer-queries, below the ~12-15 floor flagged for the other 2 domains. There was no real content available to pad this up with (same no-fabrication constraint as wta_1/world_1); flagged here for review, not silently accepted.
meta.selection_note: 104 real train-set questions covering 53 distinct gold queries (1.96x paraphrase density). Of 34 single-table candidates (weather=14, trip=10, station=9, status=1) and 19 multi-table/compound candidates, selected all 10 real trip-only questions as answer cases, plus a diverse sample of 15 refuse cases (5 weather, 4 station, 1 status -- all of it, small pool -- and 5 multi-table/compound chosen for diversity of table-pair and join/compound shape, including one trip+weather cross-theme join). No questions authored, reworded, or padded.
meta.tiers: SQL-structural (filter/aggregate/group_by/order_by/multi_or_compound), not this project's T1-T5 op-count scheme -- see eval_corpus_spider_wta_1.json's meta for the full rationale.
meta.tier_convention_note: 'tier' distinguishes answer vs refuse queries for reporting (mirrors eval_corpus.json/eval_corpus_employee.json's out_of_range convention -- never pooled into one blended accuracy number). Deliberately NOT labeled 'out_of_range': that tier means unanswerable IN PRINCIPLE (undefined terms, no such column/data at all); these refuse-cases are answerable in principle but need a table outside this domain's single-table register -- a different mechanism, kept a different label. 'sql_structure' preserves the original filter/aggregate/group_by/order_by/multi_or_compound classification for every query (answer and refuse alike).

queries.question: Give me the start station and end station for the trips with the three oldest id.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT start_station_name ,  end_station_name FROM trip ORDER BY id LIMIT 3

queries.question: What is the id of the trip that has the shortest duration?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT id FROM trip ORDER BY duration LIMIT 1

queries.question: What is the total and maximum duration of trips with bike id 636?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT sum(duration) ,  max(duration) FROM trip WHERE bike_id  =  636

queries.question: From the trip record, find the number of unique bikes.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT bike_id) FROM trip

queries.question: Which start station had the most trips starting from August? Give me the name and id of the station.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT start_station_name ,  start_station_id FROM trip WHERE start_date LIKE "8/%" GROUP BY start_station_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

queries.question: Which bike traveled the most often in zip code 94002?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT bike_id FROM trip WHERE zip_code  =  94002 GROUP BY bike_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

queries.question: Find the ids and names of stations from which at least 200 trips started.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT start_station_id ,  start_station_name FROM trip GROUP BY start_station_name HAVING COUNT(*)  >=  200

queries.question: What are the ids and durations of the trips with the top 3 durations?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT id ,  duration FROM trip ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 3

queries.question: List all the distinct stations from which a trip of duration below 100 started.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT start_station_name FROM trip WHERE duration  <  100

queries.question: Find the id for the trips that lasted at least as long as the average duration of trips in zip code 94103.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT id FROM trip WHERE duration  >=  (SELECT avg(duration) FROM trip WHERE zip_code  =  94103)

queries.question: Give me the dates when the max temperature was higher than 85.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT date FROM weather WHERE max_temperature_f  >  85
queries.reason: targets table ['weather'] -- this domain's single-table register only exposes 'trip' (matching this project's register.pkl/employees.pkl convention); the data this question needs is not visible to the system.

queries.question: What is the average bike availability in stations that are not located in Palo Alto?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT avg(bikes_available) FROM status WHERE station_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM station WHERE city  =  "Palo Alto")
queries.reason: targets table ['status'] -- this domain's single-table register only exposes 'trip' (matching this project's register.pkl/employees.pkl convention); the data this question needs is not visible to the system. queries.question: What is the latitude, longitude, city of the station from which the shortest trip started?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT T1.lat ,  T1.long ,  T1.city FROM station AS T1 JOIN trip AS T2 ON T1.id  =  T2.start_station_id ORDER BY T2.duration LIMIT 1
queries.reason: requires a multi-table join or set operation (e.g. INTERSECT); planner/'s 4 operators (filter, select, aggregate, compute) have no join or set-operation primitive. (Also references table(s) outside the single-table register.)

queries.question: What are the ids of stations that are located in San Francisco and have average bike availability above 10.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT id FROM station WHERE city  =  "San Francisco" INTERSECT SELECT station_id FROM status GROUP BY station_id HAVING avg(bikes_available)  >  10
queries.reason: requires a multi-table join or set operation (e.g. INTERSECT); planner/'s 4 operators (filter, select, aggregate, compute) have no join or set-operation primitive. (Also references table(s) outside the single-table register.)
